date_note: Guardian Audits says the FSC presented the draft on 24 November 2026.
exec: According to Guardian Audits, a Korean draft law would make digital asset businesses compensate users for hacking losses even without fault, with a possible FSC surcharge of up to 10% of revenue for security-duty breaches.
plain: Guardian Audits reports that South Korea's financial regulator presented a draft law under which crypto businesses would compensate users for hacking losses even without fault. It is still a draft.
summary: Guardian Audits reports that Korea's Financial Services Commission presented its draft digital asset law on 24 November 2026. Under it, digital asset businesses would compensate users for losses from hacking and computer-system failures even without fault. A breach of security duties that causes an incident could draw an FSC surcharge of up to 10% of revenue, Guardian Audits says.
title: Korea's FSC draft digital asset law would require no-fault compensation for hacking losses, Guardian Audits reports

validation.note: Single source: Guardian Audits (a security firm's blog). The FSC's own announcement was not found or read; a draft, not enacted.

evidence.quote: Separately, a breach of security duties that causes an incident could draw an FSC surcharge of up to 10% of revenue.

review.note: Title, 24 Nov date, no-fault compensation, 10% surcharge quote, single_source status checked against the Guardian Audits page
